notes: ACCESS: plain direct fetch worked throughout (HTTP 200, no WAF, no impersonation needed). www.schoolhouse.com 301s to schoolhouse.com; all links are canonical schoolhouse.com. PLATFORM: Shopify (Dawn 15.4.1, shop schoolhouse-development.myshopify.com). CATALOGUE SIZE IS THE HEADLINE FINDING: sitemap_products_1.xml lists only 147 product URLs site-wide, and the footer now reads 'Troy-CSL Lighting, Inc.' (Schoolhouse is under HVL Group). This is a drastically reduced catalogue versus Schoolhouse's historic assortment - the whole Lighting department is 21 products. Dozens of legacy category collections still resolve HTTP 200 but render '0 products': clocks, wall-clocks, table-clocks, new-clocks, pendants-chandeliers, chandeliers, table-lamps, shades, glass-shades, metal-shades, painted-shades, shades-by-type, exposed-bulb-fixtures, factory-lighting, utilitarian-lighting, damp-rated-lighting, art, drinkware, candles-accessories, curtain-hardware, curtains-rods, baskets, plants-with-planters, the-ceramic-collection, house-numbers-signs, mailboxes, calendars-planners, bathroom-accessories. COUNT METHOD: per memory, Shopify products_count was NOT used. Every qty is the rendered '<N> products' header on the collection page, and every one was independently confirmed by enumerating unique product slugs from the grid across ?page=1..n to exhaustion. Header == unique-slug count on 100% of the ~40 collections measured. Extra proofs: (a) all-lighting header 21 and its three nav children ceiling-lighting 7 + wall-sconce-fixtures 7 + lamps 7 = 21 with ZERO slug overlap between them - a clean disjoint partition; (b) all-hardware header 29 spans two grid pages and enumerated to exactly 29 unique slugs, proving the pagination/exhaustion check works past one page. RULE 0 GAINS: the site's live mega-menu is shallow (Lighting > Ceiling/Wall/Lamps only). Three room-named lighting branches were included that older rules would have dropped - Bathroom Lighting (12, sits under the 'Bed + Bath' menu), Bedroom Lighting (1) and Outdoor Lighting (5). All three are subsets of all-lighting (21); the overlap is the site's own taxonomy and is documented here per Rule 0.6, not a reason to skip them. 'Bathroom Mirrors' in the Bed + Bath menu points at the IDENTICAL URL /collections/mirrors as Decor > Mirrors, so it is emitted once. DE-DUPLICATION (compared by product-ID/slug sets, never by name): /collections/all-art 'Art + Wall Decor' (8) has a byte-identical slug set to /collections/mirrors (8) - dropped, Mirrors kept. /collections/porch-outdoor (5) is an identical slug set to /collections/outdoor-lighting (5) - dropped. /collections/tabletop (2) is identical to /collections/serveware-trays (2) - one row kept. /collections/kitchen-accessories (1) is a strict subset of serveware-trays - dropped. Facet re-cuts skipped: wet-rated-lighting (4), damp-rated-lighting, outdoor-covered (2), dimmable-lighting, integrated-led-*, all the shade-fitter-size collections (2.25/4/6 inch), and every in-stock-* stock filter. 'Shop all' roll-ups (all-lighting 21, all-home-decor 18, all-kitchen-dining 7, all-hardware 29) skipped as nav roll-ups. MIXED ROLL-UPS DROPPED, NOT PADDED: all-room-decor 'Room Decor' (24) reads as a decor node but its 24 slugs are 16 rugs + 8 throw pillows, i.e. 100% textiles - dropped entirely. all-kitchen-dining (7) is 2 dining tables + 3 cabinet-hardware pieces + the 2 tabletop items, so only its decorative child serveware-trays was taken. all-home-decor (18) = mirrors 8 + throw pillows 8 + the 2 tabletop items, fully covered by the kept rows. EXCLUDED: all bedding/sheets/duvets/quilts/shams/throw pillows/blankets and rugs (textiles); all furniture incl. living room, bedroom, dining, storage, outdoor furniture; drawer pulls, cabinet knobs, appliance pulls, bath hardware, door hardware, hinges, deadbolts, kick plates, towel bars/rings, paper holders (hardware/plumbing); light bulbs and ceiling fans; wallpaper; gifts; organization/utility carts and bins. INCLUDED ON THE BRIEF'S EXPLICIT 'decorative hooks, decorative wall racks/shelves' allowance: Hooks + Racks (8) and Shelves + Ledges (1), the two children of the Wall Hardware nav node (9 = 8 + 1 exactly) - these are Schoolhouse's signature decorative brass wall hooks, not cabinet hardware. DATA-QUALITY FLAG: /collections/outdoor-lighting reports 5 products but one of the 5 grid tiles is 'lisse-rug', an outdoor rug mis-tagged into the lighting collection (it is likewise the 2nd of 2 items in outdoor-covered). The qty recorded is the site's own reported 5 per the exact-qty rule, flagged accordingly. CLOCKS: explicitly in scope this batch and Schoolhouse is historically known for its IBM/wall clocks, so the node is reported rather than silently omitted - /collections/clocks is live and renders literally '0 products'. qty 0 is what the site reports.
